short: The lead ship of her formidable carrier class, Shokaku was a veteran of the Pearl Harbor attack and early Pacific clashes.
full:
Commissioned in August 1941, Shokaku was a fast, heavily armed, and highly capable fleet carrier that formed the backbone of Japanese naval aviation alongside her sister ship Zuikaku. She participated in the Pearl Harbor strike and supported Japanese offensives across the Pacific. At the Battle of the Coral Sea, Shokaku suffered severe bomb damage that prevented her from participating in the disastrous Battle of Midway.

Shokaku frequently bore the brunt of American counterattacks in subsequent engagements, including the grueling Solomon Islands campaign. Her career ended at the Battle of the Philippine Sea in June 1944. While launching strikes against the American fleet, she was torpedoed by the submarine USS Cavalla. The hit ignited aviation fuel fumes, causing a catastrophic explosion that tore the ship apart.
